messages:
maya: Quick report from canary: bringing up melusine-13b-v2 (int4) — seeing reproducible OOMs under mixed context lengths. hits ~2m into run when some requests have 1200+ context + long gen.

tri: can you paste the minimal repro?

maya: yes. local canary command: `./canary --model melusine-13b-v2-int4 --scenario news-summarize --qps 30 --concurrency 10 --max_new_tokens 200 --batching windowed` then after ~110s process dies. log: ```
E0415 10:11:12 cuda_allocator.cpp:329] cudaMalloc(8192MB) failed: out of memory
memstats: free_runs=48 largest_contig=5.3GiB total_free=16.4GiB small_chunks=46
```

josh: small_chunks high -> fragmentation. did you try compacting heuristics?

maya: tried `slot_compactor=true` in runtime and OOMs stopped in local runs. p50 throughput dropped 8% but stable at qps 40.

emma: interesting — any effect of `max_new_tokens`?

maya: yes, reducing to 96 also prevents the OOM consistently and keeps p50 closer to baseline. with 200 we hit the cliff.

tri: hypothesis: windowed batching + kv_prefetch aggressively allocates large contiguous KV slabs when long-gen tasks arrive, causing allocator to fragment. two mitigations: lower max_new_tokens default and enable slot compactor or reduce prefetch.

josh: suggestions: 1) ship model defaults: max_new_tokens=96, kv_prefetch=false, slot_compactor=true; 2) add routing fallback to melusine-13b-int8 when canary OOM rate > 0.5 per 5m; 3) add perf gate — if int4 ROUGE-L < float16 ROUGE-L -1.5 then hold.

emma: did we run quality evals?

eval-bot: quick sweep results (summarization subset, 1200 prompts): float16 baseline ROUGE-L=35.4, int4 candidate ROUGE-L=32.8, int8 variant ROUGE-L=35.1. latency p99: float16 420ms, int4 380ms, int8 410ms.

maya: int4 quality drop is larger than acceptable. suspects: outlier clipping aggressive in current 4-bit pipeline.

tri: can we try symmetric per-channel with per-block outlier capture or mixed 5-bit in head-layers? run a small eval with 200 prompts to see deltas.

josh: also try enabling `compaction_threshold=0.6` in runtime so we compact when fragmentation ratio > 0.6. that reduced free small chunks in my tests.

maya: minimal runtime override I used for safer canary: ```json
{"model":"melusine-13b-v2-int4","defaults":{"max_new_tokens":"96","kv_prefetch":"false","slot_compactor":"true","compaction_threshold":"0.6","batch_window_ms":"40"}}
```

tri: thanks. open a PR with that and add a canary slow-start (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 12h). also add an automated metric: if allocator.small_chunks > 40 and largest_contig < 6GiB then reduce concurrency or roll back.

josh: filed INF-2729 for allocator tuning and a kernel lazy-load experiment — assigned @mike.

emma: follow-up QA: after applying the runtime defaults in canary for 3h spike (qps 45) we saw 0 OOMs, fragmentation small_chunks dropped from median 48->22, largest_contig increased ~0.8GiB. int4 ROUGE-L remained ~32.9. int8 still 35.1.

maya: conclusion: safety defaults prevent production OOMs but int4 quality unacceptable for now. plan: revert int4 production enablement, keep defaults for frag safety, iterate on quant pipeline (outlier-aware symmetric, per-head scaling, try 5-bit mapping), and prepare a targeted eval of 5-bit/affine schemes.

tri: est next steps: - PR with defaults + canary gating (#4599) - small quant experiments (maya/josh) - allocator INF-2729 investigation (infra) - hold production int4 until quality gate passes.

emma: 👍 also add a note to the model onboarding checklist to run fragmentation stress test (mixed context lengths up to 1536, long gens) before enabling aggressive prefetch.

maya: posted PR #4599 with artifacts: p50/p95/p99, memmaps, and reproducible harness.

eval-bot: kicked off targeted 5-bit vs 4-bit eval (2000 prompts). ETA 1h.

tri: thanks everyone. ping me if the 5-bit sweep shows parity to float16.
